cells.tense: You are here with the pen, holding two demands in one steady hand.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Pick a job you'd normally finish quietly and do its next step where the person it's for can see you working. Say nothing about it.
cells.core:
You can carry two things at once without dropping either. The work you do for people is steady and shaped, and most of it happens where nobody watches. What you've built is real, and some of it has sat finished for a while without you standing beside it and calling it done.

Try one move this week. Take a piece of what you do for someone and do the next step where they can see you at it. Not for thanks. So the effort you spend has a witness once. You don't have to mention what it costs you. Let one afternoon be ordinary and visible instead of private and unpaid, then leave whatever they make of it with them.
cells.sheetLine: You carry two demands at once and nobody sees the work.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care, both demands kept in hand
cells.place: where you bear what has to be borne without hardening

cells.tense: You will be braced for what hasn't happened yet, gripping a form nobody asked you to hold.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Eat the meal you cooked or use the thing you fixed for ten minutes without improving it or starting the next job.
cells.core:
Your grip tightens sooner than the thing itself arrives. You're holding next season's shape before it's grown, braced for demands that haven't come, and the bracing has stopped being strength and become clutch. The work you tend is fine. You keep holding it after the job is done, and nothing gets set down, yourself included.

This week, take something already finished and let its plain fact land. Eat the meal, use the room you built, and change nothing about any of it for ten minutes. Whatever you thought finishing would feel like — go there now that it is finished. That isn't idleness. It's the part of tending that lets a piece of work be done rather than forever one step short.

cells.tense: You were carrying it, and at some point the load came down.
cells.act: go on toward it without needing a sign
cells.ask: Go back to the aim you once chose here and take one step toward it this week, with no proof it will work.
cells.core:
The knack for tending is still in you; it just isn't moving. What you used to keep going for has gone silent, and the silence reads like it's over, though the strength to bear things hasn't left. Nothing new has been picked up, and the old weight is off your shoulders.

Don't push at the hollow. Go back to the smallest version of the aim you once chose. One step toward it this week, no sign, no proof it will work, no plan beyond the step itself. Persistence doesn't return by force. It returns by moving once toward something you still hope for, and finding the strength was only waiting for a direction to point at.

cells.tense: You are holding several lives in shape while telling yourself you had no hand in it.
cells.act: stand where the giving can be witnessed
cells.ask: Do part of what you set aside for someone where they can watch, and skip explaining what it cost you.
cells.core:
You keep things standing and the story you tell is that you were just standing there. The work is yours. The credit stayed on the table, and the people being held level have had a clear view of it the whole time. What you do isn't invisible to anyone except the one doing it, and the not-seeing is what costs, not the doing.

One move this week. Let somebody who benefits from what you set aside watch you do part of it — quietly, no explanation, no asking them to notice. Then what you spent stops being a hidden cost and becomes something that happened between two people. If they thank you, take it in rather than brushing past. The release you're after sits on the far side of being seen, not the far side of more work.
cells.sheetLine: The balance is kept by you, and you say you're just standing there.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care, both demands kept in hand
cells.place: where you bear what has to be borne without hardening
